description: A plant manager must authorize the use of a reclaimed polymer lot for a medical-device housing run and finalize the blend, inspection, storage, and waste controls, with input from a quality engineer and an environmental compliance specialist.

shared_context.S1: The medical-device housing run is scheduled for Thursday, and the available virgin polymer is insufficient to complete the planned batch.
shared_context.S2: A lot of reclaimed polymer pellets is available in the materials cage and has not yet been authorized for this product.
shared_context.S3: Mara makes the final authorization decision, and the plant normally records material approval, inspection, storage, and waste controls before a regulated-product run begins.
shared_context.S4: Before finalizing the run plan, Mara conducts the routine quality and environmental-compliance check-in with Jon and Priya.

PF1.text: Jon's completed lab review shows the reclaimed polymer is suitable for this housing only at a 15% reclaimed-to-85% virgin blend; he also confirmed that the first 50 molded housings must receive FTIR identity testing, but the lab result has not yet been attached to the production traveler.

PF2.text: Priya's review of the supplier's revised safety data sheet, received late yesterday and not yet entered in the plant's chemical register, classifies the reclaimed lot's additive residue as regulated process waste, requiring labeled segregated storage and a hazardous-waste manifest for any discarded pellets or purge material.

acceptance_conditions: The reclaimed polymer must be authorized at exactly a 15% blend.
The first exactly 50 housings must receive FTIR identity testing.
The reclaimed material must be placed in segregated labeled storage.
Discarded reclaimed pellets or purge material must be handled through a hazardous-waste manifest.
The material authorization record must be completed before the run.
The quality finding must be cited by the decision-maker as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The lab review changes the blend from an unspecified or generic reclaimed-material use to exactly 15% reclaimed polymer and changes inspection to FTIR testing on exactly the first 50 housings.
The revised safety data sheet changes storage from ordinary materials-cage storage to segregated labeled storage and changes disposal to a hazardous-waste manifest.
